cells.tense: You are inside a connection you actually chose, and what you are tending with it is still in the middle of becoming.
cells.ask: Give what is growing one more day of your full attention before you decide what it is turning into.
cells.core:
Tending something still developing looks like this when it is going well: you stay in real contact with it, you notice what it is becoming, and you let it take the time it needs instead of pulling it toward a shape you picked in advance. You are doing that here. The connection is being met rather than managed, and the growth is running out of the meeting itself. Nothing is being forced. What you are growing gets to arrive at its own speed.

What holds it steady is that you chose it, and you keep choosing it. The momentum does not rest on your shoulders, and it does not need defending. The tending comes back to you as something that keeps getting more itself, and as a person who can feel the difference.
cells.sheetLine: You chose this connection and you are tending it as it grows.
cells.verb: Choosing a connection and letting two streams run as one
cells.place: In the part of life that tends what is still growing

cells.tense: You are already living a version of this that has not happened, and arranging everyone else around that picture.
cells.ask: Leave one outcome open this week and let someone else's reading of it stand.
cells.core:
Care for a growing thing at its best looks like patient attention: you bring water and light, you watch what changes, and then you step back, and the thing does its own developing in its own time. Right now the stepping back is missing. You have a finished picture of how this turns out and you are working backward from it, so the closeness has become a schedule you are running. You are ahead of everything that is actually here.

The care is not the problem. The grip is. Loosening it — letting the thing grow at the speed it is actually growing — is what brings the connection back into the present, where it can reach you.
cells.sheetLine: You are rearranging the present around a future you have already decided.
cells.verb: Choosing a connection and letting two streams run as one
cells.place: In the part of life that tends what is still growing

cells.tense: You stopped bringing what you see into the care of what is growing, and you are still standing where you stopped.
cells.ask: Put one clear sentence about what is growing in front of someone this week, and let their reply land.
cells.core:
The good version of this seat is direct attention: you watch the thing develop, you trust what you notice, and you let that noticing guide the care you give it. You still watch. What has gone is the saying — what you see about this thing stays inside and never reaches anyone or anything. The caring continues, but it is running on half the information.

The seeing did not leave. The offering did. Handing one clear impression to someone — not a verdict, just what is true for you — lets the next thing arrive on its own. A steady ground shows up under you once it is spoken.
cells.sheetLine: You see something about what is growing and you are not voicing it.
cells.verb: Choosing a connection and letting two streams run as one
cells.place: In the part of life that tends what is still growing

cells.tense: You are already making the choices this connection rests on, and describing them as though they made themselves.
cells.ask: Tomorrow, tell one person plainly that you picked this, and let the sentence stand without softening it.
cells.core:
Tending well looks like this: you are present to what is developing, you respond to what it needs, and the whole thing carries your stamp. That is happening here. You keep the thing watered and you keep it safe, and you do it with your own hands every day. It is not luck and it is not just how things went.

The one thing missing is the acknowledgment. You keep saying it worked itself out, as if the shape of it belonged to no one. Claiming the choosing as yours is what lets the next step be deliberate rather than inevitable, and it gives the care the weight it has earned.
cells.sheetLine: You are already deciding this, and calling it nobody's choice.
cells.verb: Choosing a connection and letting two streams run as one
cells.place: In the part of life that tends what is still growing
